The 2026-08-26 spiral-ham ruling refused deli-ham for a 7-9 lb bone-in roast, which is the opposite case and supports this one. Board 7 of 7 at 0.1238.

Fully cooked, seasoned shredded pork sold refrigerated (Del Real, Curly's); board ABSENT and no vocabulary row shares a core word. Nulling would pantry-price 280 g of the recipe's second meat, so it goes to the registrar as a new id rather than being bridged onto a raw pork cut.
Exact vocabulary row Dill Pickle Slices [pickles], same form; board 7 of 7 at 0.05, and the 2026-08-26 pickle-brine ruling already treats jarred dill pickles as this id.

REFUSED the board's sliced-cheese bridge: at 0.145/oz that id is the generic American-class sandwich slice, while Swiss is variety-priced, exactly like the red-onion vs onions precedent. Slicing is a knife cut of the same cheese, so the vocabulary's swiss-cheese id is a reuse, not a form flip. new_commodity_proposals.evidence: Fully cooked, seasoned shredded pork sold in refrigerated heat-and-serve pouches (Del Real 15 oz, Curly's, store-brand carnitas), roughly $6-8/lb - a different product concept and price class from any raw pork cut, so it cannot reuse pork-loin, pork-shoulder or ground-pork, and it is not deli-ham or diced-ham. The pre-resolve table reports board ABSENT for the term: no commodity match and no capture match across the estate's three commodity namespaces, and no vocabulary row shares a core word with it. If the estate already prices a cooked pulled-pork product under another spelling (pulled-pork, carnitas, cooked-pork), alias to that instead - that pairing is exactly the word-order/synonym case audit-commodity-dupes cannot catch. This recipe's method puts 1/2 cup on each breast, 280 g at source scale and 980 g at the 14-serving batch, so a null here would pantry-price over 2 lb of meat.
